rows.locus: two methods, candidate keyword-only and REQUIRED on submit_proposal
rows.divergence: no defensible alternative: section 2 gives both exact signatures, and P01 expressly fixes method count, keyword kind, and requiredness
rows.distinguishing_probe: n/a
rows.proposed: Implement both signatures verbatim; let Python argument binding own omitted-candidate and unexpected-keyword failures.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Both signatures ship verbatim; `candidate` is keyword-only and required, and argument binding owns omission and unexpected keywords. No body-level validator exists.

rows.locus: both return the proposal ID as a bare str, no new model
rows.divergence: Reading A requires type(result) is the built-in str; reading B accepts any str subclass because isinstance(result, str) holds. Both can be described as a bare str while exposing different runtime types.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Register one operation, submit one valid direct candidate, and run one valid source-backed call. Observe type(result) is str, result == the inserted proposals.id, and no dataclass or str subclass escapes.
rows.proposed: The words 'bare str' plus the rejection of a model mandate the exact built-in str carrying the proposal ID; pin type(result) is str for both methods.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `type(result) is str`, not a subclass, for both methods. No new model.
rows.contract_action: none - section 12 V-P02 already carries it

rows.locus: submit_proposal NEVER invokes a source, even when one is configured and raising
rows.divergence: Reading A forbids only calling candidate_source.propose; reading B treats 'must not affect it' as forbidding even retrieval or validation of the configured source on the direct path. A hostile descriptor separates them.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Construct System with a source whose propose property is initially callable, then arm that property to count and raise on attribute retrieval. Call submit_proposal with a valid operation and Candidate; observe success plus zero retrievals versus an access-triggered failure.
rows.proposed: The contract mandates zero source calls. Because it also says the configured source must not affect direct submission, recommend that submit_proposal neither read nor validate self.candidate_source after construction.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `submit_proposal` never reads `self.candidate_source`. A configured source that raises on every call cannot affect it, because the attribute is never touched.

rows.locus: propose invokes self.candidate_source and nothing else; no per-call source argument
rows.divergence: Reading A snapshots self.candidate_source once and invokes that object; reading B checks one value for None and later re-reads the attribute, so reassignment or a stateful descriptor can select another source. The contract does not state snapshot semantics.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Use a System subclass whose armed candidate_source getter returns source A on its first read and source B on its second. Call propose for a valid operation; record getter count and which source received the sole CandidateRequest.
rows.proposed: The contract requires the configured System source and no per-call authority. It is silent on reassignment races; recommend one local snapshot whose None check and exactly-one invocation bind the same object.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED and EXTENDED by X09. `propose` snapshots the attribute into one local, so the `None` check and the single invocation bind the same object. Reassignment mid-call cannot split them. Unusable non-`None` configuration is contained, not pre-validated.
rows.contract_action: section 5 publishes the snapshot rule and X09's containment boundary

rows.locus: neither name is exported from __init__.py; reachable only through System
rows.divergence: Reading A means only that submit_proposal and propose are absent from __all__; reading B means cement_runtime has no top-level attributes with those names at all. A module alias can satisfy A while violating 'only through System'.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Import cement_runtime, then observe both name in cement_runtime.__all__ and hasattr(cement_runtime, name) for submit_proposal and propose; separately observe callable attributes on System. Reading B requires false, false, and true respectively.
rows.proposed: 'Only through System' and '__init__.py gains no new symbol' mandate no module attributes and no __all__ entries for either method name; expose them solely as System methods.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Neither name is in `__all__` nor a module attribute; both are reachable only as `System` methods.

rows.locus: handle's bytes stay identical to 1182130a2b3a, 12,866 B by AST slice
rows.divergence: no defensible alternative: the contract names the AST-delimited function, excludes its terminal newline, and supplies both a byte count and SHA-256 prefix
rows.distinguishing_probe: n/a
rows.proposed: Slice System.handle through ast.FunctionDef end_lineno, remove its one terminal LF, and require 12,866 bytes with SHA-256 prefix 1182130a2b3a; do not edit the function.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, with the convention named. `handle` is byte-identical across the unit. The figure reproduces only under the whole-line span from `lineno` to `end_lineno` with trailing newlines stripped: 12,866 B / `1182130a2b3a`. `ast.get_source_segment` drops the four-space indent and gives 12,862 B / `c27e71b0b4c7`. 'AST slice' alone is ambiguous by exactly those four bytes.
rows.contract_action: section 12 MEASUREMENT states the convention with both figures

rows.locus: success footprint: exactly one requests row, one proposals row, one events row, nothing else
rows.divergence: Reading A quantifies only Cement's declared schema tables; reading B quantifies every SQLite table, including sqlite_sequence. Because events.sequence is AUTOINCREMENT, every success necessarily mutates sqlite_sequence and makes reading B impossible.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Snapshot every name returned by SELECT name FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type='table', including sqlite_sequence, before and after one valid direct submission. Compare row deltas: three Cement tables change, while sqlite_sequence also advances for events.
rows.proposed: The feasible reading is exactly three Cement-owned table deltas, with SQLite-maintained sequence state excluded. Clarify that domain; still compare every declared SCHEMA table so an accidental application-table write fails.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED. The footprint quantifies over Cement's DECLARED SCHEMA tables. `events.sequence` is AUTOINCREMENT, so every success necessarily mutates `sqlite_sequence`; a reading covering every SQLite table is unsatisfiable and would fail against correct code.

rows.locus: the request row is written directly as pending with proposal_id set and no lease
rows.divergence: Reading A permits omitting attempts from the INSERT and relying on its schema default of 1; reading B requires the INSERT statement to supply attempts=1 explicitly. The persisted row is identical, but SQL tracing distinguishes them.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Trace SQL for one valid direct call and inspect the inserted request row. Observe whether attempts appears in the INSERT column list while the final row still has status pending, proposal_id set, both lease columns NULL, and attempts 1.
rows.proposed: The contract mandates the persisted row shape and forbids any generating state; it does not mandate spelling a defaulted column in SQL. Recommend accepting either INSERT form while pinning no generating INSERT or UPDATE occurs.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The request row is written directly as `pending` with `proposal_id` set. No lease column is written and no generating state exists. Spelling a defaulted column in SQL was never mandated; the persisted row shape is.

rows.locus: the event is proposal.created; payload and subject match handle's write MINUS request identity
rows.divergence: Reading A subtracts only the payload request_id key from handle's current event, yielding payload {}; reading B also treats partition or sequence correlation as request identity and changes more fields. The phrase 'any request identity' does not enumerate the retained event columns.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Capture handle's baseline proposal.created event and a new submission event for equivalent content. Normalize generated IDs and compare kind, partition, subject_type, subject_id, payload, created_at_us, and sequence; observe whether only payload.request_id was removed.
rows.proposed: The baseline has request identity only in payload.request_id. Mandate kind proposal.created, subject_type proposal, subject_id equal to the returned proposal ID, payload {}, and the ordinary partition/time/sequence columns unchanged in meaning.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. kind `proposal.created`, subject_type `proposal`, subject_id equal to the returned proposal ID, payload `{}`. Request identity is absent, which is the one delta from `handle`'s write.

rows.locus: no caller-supplied identifier; byte-identical content submitted twice writes two of everything
rows.divergence: Reading A guarantees distinct IDs under the unmodified UUID generator; reading B treats the unconditional 'produces ... distinct proposal IDs' as requiring collision recovery when the internal generator repeats. Ordinary duplicate-content probes cannot separate them.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Patch _new_id so two valid duplicate submissions receive distinct request IDs but the same proposed prop ID. Observe whether the second call regenerates and succeeds with a distinct proposal ID or raises a uniqueness/integrity failure.
rows.proposed: The contract unconditionally mandates two successful rows, events, and distinct proposal IDs for ordinary duplicate submissions. It is silent on injected generator collisions; recommend qualifying the domain to the runtime UUID generator rather than adding retry semantics here.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. No caller-supplied identifier exists on either signature. Byte-identical content submitted twice writes two requests, two proposals, two events, and returns two distinct IDs.

rows.locus: propose invokes the source exactly once on success and exactly zero times on every raising path
rows.divergence: Reading A constrains successful calls only and permits an internal retry after a source exception; reading B combines section 7's 'source raises' rows with D05 and requires exactly one invocation on every call that reaches the source, including failures.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Use a source that increments a counter, raises RuntimeError with a secret on call one, and would return a valid Candidate on call two. Call propose and observe CandidateSourceError with count 1 versus a retried success with count 2.
rows.proposed: Section 7 makes the first raised source exception the call's public failure, so the contract as a whole mandates one invocation whenever invocation begins. Add that sentence to D05; retain zero calls for all pre-invocation failures.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Exactly one invocation on success. Zero on every failure that precedes invocation. The persistence seam never re-invokes, so a revision-race failure after generation still counts one.

rows.locus: one private persistence seam writes the request row, the proposal row and the event for both paths
rows.divergence: Reading A requires one private helper that contains all three writes and is called by both public methods; reading B accepts three shared row-level helpers or duplicated public-method SQL because the runtime footprint remains identical. Behavioural probes alone cannot distinguish them.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Parse system.py, locate every requests INSERT, proposals INSERT, and proposal.created _event call added by M3.3, then walk callers. Reading A has one private method owning all three sites and both public methods reaching that one method.
rows.proposed: The structural words 'ONE private persistence seam' and 'single writer' mandate reading A. Pin the AST call graph as well as differential behaviour; a composition of separate writers does not satisfy this obligation.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED as STRUCTURAL, not behavioural. `_persist_proposal` contains all three writes and is the sole writer for both paths. Three shared row-level helpers would produce an identical footprint, so the pin is a call-graph spy, not a footprint comparison.

rows.locus: validation order: partition, operation, input_value canonicalization, then candidate
rows.divergence: Reading A treats the four-item list as a total order that needs one probe per adjacent edge; reading B treats D08's partition-versus-input spanning pair as sufficient, leaving operation versus input and input versus candidate free to swap.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Make three DIRECT fixtures: bad partition + bad operation; bad operation + non-JSON input; non-JSON input + malformed candidate. Assert the first listed validator wins each pair, with zero transaction and source counts. Repeat the first two applicable edges through propose.
rows.proposed: The words 'in this order' mandate every adjacent edge: partition before operation, operation before input canonicalization, and input before direct-candidate validation. Add all three pairwise probes rather than relying on D08.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED as a TOTAL order needing one probe per ADJACENT edge: partition before operation, operation before input canonicalization, input before candidate canonicalization.

rows.locus: a bad partition together with a bad input_value reports the PARTITION error
rows.divergence: no defensible alternative: D08 names both invalid arguments, the winning error, and its resolve precedent, while D07 applies that order to both public methods
rows.distinguishing_probe: n/a
rows.proposed: For both submit_proposal and propose, combine an invalid partition with a value of type object; require the existing partition ValidationError before canonicalization, transaction entry, or source invocation.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED but NOT load-bearing. The partition/input pair SPANS two edges and pins neither interior one. It is a sample of D07, which carries the obligation.
rows.contract_action: section 4 records that D07's adjacent-edge probes subsume D08

rows.locus: a rejected call performs zero transactions and zero source invocations, measured with live spies
rows.divergence: Reading A limits 'rejected call' to argument-validation rejection in section 4; reading B covers every call that raises. Reading B conflicts with D12's operation-read transaction, D21's lookup, and source failures that occur after one invocation.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Run live transaction and source spies over three fixtures: bad partition, unregistered operation, and a raising source. Reading A expects (0,0), (1,0), and (at least 1,1); reading B incorrectly expects zeroes for all.
rows.proposed: Context and the rest of the contract mandate reading A. Rewrite D09 as 'a call rejected by argument validation' and retain positive controls for both transaction and source counters.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED to a call rejected by ARGUMENT VALIDATION. Read wider it contradicts D12's read transaction, D21's operation lookup, and every failure that follows one source invocation.

rows.locus: omitted candidate and passing source= both raise Python's own TypeError; no shipped validator
rows.divergence: Reading A freezes the exact CPython text observed by the test environment; reading B requires only native signature binding, whose wording may vary across supported Python versions. The contract explicitly permits a test to pin text but does not publish that text.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Under each supported Python minor, call submit_proposal without candidate and pass source= to both methods before constructing a ledger fixture. Record type, exact str(exc), traceback origin, and zero method-body spy calls; compare wording across interpreters.
rows.proposed: The shipped obligation is native TypeError from the exact signatures, with no method-body validator. A repository test may pin the current gate interpreter's text, but that text is not a cross-version public Cement message.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Omitted `candidate` and an unexpected `source=` both raise Python's own `TypeError`. No shipped validator produces those; the exact signatures do.

rows.locus: the source runs outside every open transaction; no connection reports in_transaction
rows.divergence: Reading A requires zero Cement connections to remain open during source execution; reading B permits idle open connections but requires in_transaction false on each. Split measured four open idle connections, while XOR measured zero, and both were accepted.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Inject a connection factory that retains every live connection and proves in_transaction true during a positive-control write. During a blocking source call, record both live-connection count and each in_transaction value; an idle retained connection separates A from B.
rows.proposed: The second sentence and accepted split measurement mandate reading B: no Cement-held connection may be in a transaction. Recommend closing unused connections anyway, but do not silently strengthen this into a zero-open-connection contract.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, reading B: no Cement-held connection may be IN A TRANSACTION while the source runs. Idle open connections are permitted. `propose` invokes the source between two closed transactions, so the pin observes every connection Cement opens and carries a positive control.

rows.locus: the operation revision is read before invocation and re-read inside the write transaction
rows.divergence: Reading A applies the two-read race guard only to propose, because only that path invokes a source with a captured revision; reading B makes submit_proposal perform the same pre-read and re-read through D06's shared seam. The direct candidate carries no captured revision.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Trace transactions and scoped operation SELECTs for one valid direct call and one valid source-backed call. Reading A yields one operation read inside the direct write but a pre-invocation read plus an in-write re-read for propose; reading B yields two for both.
rows.proposed: Section 5 mandates the two-read guard for propose only. Recommend that submit_proposal validate the operation once inside its atomic write transaction; the shared persistence seam receives the direct path's revision from that locked read.
rows.main_verdict: CHANGED THE SHIPPED CODE. The pre-read/re-read guard belongs to `propose` ALONE. MAIN's first implementation gave both paths a pre-read plus a seam re-read for symmetry; a direct caller captures no revision, so a concurrent `revise_operation` raised `StateError` for a submission with no generation window to protect. SHIPPED: `expected_revision: int | None`; `submit_proposal` passes `None` and opens exactly ONE transaction.
rows.contract_action: section 5 D12 scoped to the source path; section 12 V-D12 carries the full record

rows.locus: the revision re-read uses a scoped query; reusing System.operations() is rejected
rows.divergence: Reading A scopes only the selected row by partition and name, so SELECT * is allowed; reading B also scopes the projected columns and permits only SELECT revision. Both avoid materializing the partition's other operations.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Register two operations in one partition, trace SQL during propose, and inspect the in-write re-read. Compare SELECT * FROM operations WHERE partition=? AND name=? with SELECT revision using the same predicates; also fail any unscoped operations() call.
rows.proposed: The contract mandates row scope, not a column projection. Either query satisfies D13, but recommend SELECT revision because that is the only consumed value and best matches the stated census purpose.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Row scope is mandatory; column projection is not. `SELECT revision` ships because it is the only consumed value. Reusing `System.operations()` stays rejected: it returns the whole partition.

rows.locus: propose hands the source a CandidateRequest carrying the generated internal request ID
rows.divergence: The acceptance contract mandates retaining CandidateRequest.request_id for M3.3, while m3u3-map.json S01 says M3.3 must remove that field. A competent implementer following the map produces a different protocol object from one following the controlling contract.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Use a recording source, call propose once, fetch the inserted request row by the returned proposal, and inspect dataclasses.fields(CandidateRequest). Require a request_id field whose value equals the generated internal requests.id.
rows.proposed: The contract is authoritative and explicitly marks the field transitional until M3.5b. Retain and populate request_id in M3.3; MAIN should record m3u3-map.json S01 as stale rather than following it.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. `CandidateRequest.request_id` is retained and populated with the generated internal ID, transitional until M3.5b. `m3u3-map.json` S01 says M3.3 removes it; that row is STALE and superseded, not followed.

rows.locus: a failed submission leaves the ledger byte-identical under four independent pins
rows.divergence: Reading A compares an isolated failure's before/after ledger, excluding mutations deliberately committed by another actor; reading B applies byte identity across the revision-race fixture. B is impossible because the concurrent operation.revised event legitimately changes the file and dump.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Block the source, snapshot the ledger, revise the operation, snapshot again, then release the source and snapshot after propose raises. The first-to-final comparison changes; the post-revision-to-final comparison must preserve request/proposal counts, proposal.created count and sequence, file SHA-256, and full iterdump.
rows.proposed: D15 must mean zero submission-attributable mutation. For isolated failures compare call entry to exit; for injected concurrent mutation compare immediately after the injector commits to after the rejected submission completes. Keep all four assertion groups independent.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED to zero SUBMISSION-ATTRIBUTABLE mutation. The revision-race fixture's own source commits an operation revision, so an unconditional 'ledger byte-identical' reading is false for a correct implementation. Isolated failures compare call entry to exit; injected concurrent mutation compares against the post-injection state.
rows.contract_action: section 6 restates D15 in the attributable form

rows.locus: zero commit() calls on any failure path, measured through a connect-factory spy
rows.divergence: Reading A covers failures raised before Store.transaction reaches its commit branch; reading B includes commit itself failing. B is unsatisfiable: a Connection subclass whose commit() increments then raises creates a failed call with one commit invocation.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Inject a Connection subclass whose commit counter increments and whose submission-write commit raises sqlite3.OperationalError. Compare that fixture with validation, missing-source, source-error, and revision-race failures; the injected commit failure raises after count 1 while pre-commit failures stay at 0.
rows.proposed: Limit the zero-call obligation to every ruled failure that occurs before commit, or restate it as zero successful submission commits on any failure. Do not claim zero commit() invocations when commit is the failing operation.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED to failures occurring BEFORE commit. A `commit()` that itself raises is one invocation and no reading can forbid it. Equivalent restatement: zero SUCCESSFUL submission commits on any failure path.

rows.locus: neither method reads the clock except through self._now nor consults artifact/example/function tables
rows.divergence: Reading A permits any number of self._now calls and therefore different request, proposal, and event timestamps; reading B treats the shared identical persistence seam as one completed-time snapshot for all three rows. D17 fixes the clock source but not call count.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Use a clock that returns a distinct increasing value on every call. Submit once through each method, record self._now count and every created_at_us/updated_at_us value, and trace SELECT table names to detect artifact, example, receipt, or membership reads.
rows.proposed: As written, only the clock source and forbidden tables are mandatory. Recommend one self._now call after a candidate is available, passed into the shared seam for all submission timestamps; pin the call count if identical timestamps are intended.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. The clock source is mandatory; the call count is not. One `self._now()` inside the write transaction, shared by all three rows, is what ships - the M3.1 ruling that a clock read ahead of the authoritative plan can commit a row older than its own build.

rows.locus: both source-failure rows raise from None; no class, message, cause, context or frame reaches the caller
rows.divergence: Reading A assumes raise CandidateSourceError(...) from None inside the except block clears context; reading B inspects __context__ directly. Python suppresses display in A but still retains the adapter exception object, class, message, and traceback through __context__.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Raise a secret-bearing custom exception inside a source frame. Catch the public CandidateSourceError and inspect __cause__, __context__, __suppress_context__, repr, str, and every frame reachable from both the public traceback and chained exceptions. Require no adapter object or frame reachable.
rows.proposed: The explicit context prohibition mandates reading B. Catch and discard the adapter exception, exit the except block, then raise CandidateSourceError('candidate source failed') from None so both __cause__ and __context__ are None.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, reading B, with the mechanism named. `raise ... from None` INSIDE an `except` block leaves `__context__` populated with the adapter's exception, so reading A fails its own prohibition. The seam discards the exception, EXITS the handler, and raises there, where `__context__` is genuinely `None`. It keeps `from None` so both readings hold.

rows.locus: the two source-failure rows are indistinguishable to the caller
rows.divergence: Reading A limits indistinguishability to the public exception projection enumerated by D18; reading B includes every caller observation. B is impossible because the caller supplies the adapter and can set a flag, vary timing, or retain the exact exception before raising it.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Use one caller-owned source that records which branch it took before raising CandidateSourceError or RuntimeError. Compare public exception class/text/chain/frames and separately inspect the source's retained flag. Public projections can match while the caller-owned flag distinguishes branches.
rows.proposed: Constrain D19 to observations through the raised Cement exception: class, message, repr, cause, context, and traceback. The contract cannot hide facts already known through caller-owned adapter state or timing.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED to observations THROUGH the raised Cement exception: class, message, repr, cause, context, frames. The caller owns the adapter and can always instrument it directly; no library can hide that.

rows.locus: failure raises; it never returns a value and never writes request.fallback_failed or a failed row
rows.divergence: no defensible alternative: section 7 explicitly replaces handle's returned and persisted fallback state with exception semantics, and section 6 independently forbids a durable failure footprint
rows.distinguishing_probe: n/a
rows.proposed: For every ruled submission failure, assert that the call raises, returns no sentinel or Outcome, writes no failed request, and emits no request.fallback_failed event; leave handle's legacy behavior unchanged.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. Every ruled failure raises. No sentinel, no `Outcome`, no `failed` request row, no `request.fallback_failed` event. Those belong to `handle`, which keeps them.

rows.locus: NotFoundError for an unregistered operation is raised BEFORE the source is invoked
rows.divergence: no defensible alternative: the condition, exact precedence, error class and source-call observation are all explicit, and D12 independently requires the pre-invocation operation read
rows.distinguishing_probe: n/a
rows.proposed: Call propose with valid arguments and an unregistered operation using a live source counter; require the exact T05 NotFoundError, one scoped read transaction, zero source calls, and no ledger mutation.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, and ORDERED by X03. `NotFoundError` precedes invocation, after one scoped read transaction. It does NOT precede the missing-configuration check: with `candidate_source is None` and an unregistered operation, `propose` raises `StateError` having opened zero transactions.

rows.locus: neither the return value nor the proposal.created event publishes the request identifier
rows.divergence: Reading A forbids inline publication in those two values only; reading B forbids transitive discovery from the returned proposal ID. D23 explicitly says get_proposal is an immediate discovery path, so B would contradict the next obligation.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Submit once, inspect the bare returned string and every event field recursively, then call get_proposal with that string. Reading A permits the final ProposalView.request_id discovery while requiring no request ID in the return or event itself.
rows.proposed: The contract mandates reading A: return only proposal_id and emit payload {} with no request ID. State explicitly that 'publishes' is channel-local, because the unchanged read API still exposes the binding transitively.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, reading A, CHANNEL-LOCAL. 'Publishes' covers the return value and the event: return only `proposal_id`, emit payload `{}`. D23's `get_proposal` route is transitive discovery through an authorized reader and is not a violation.

rows.locus: the contract publishes the eight live seams that still expose the identifier rather than claiming privacy
rows.divergence: Reading A counts the union of eight named high-level API/protocol seams; reading B claims an exhaustive count of every live route. B omits direct database access and System.store, and it also fails per-path because DIRECT does not invoke CandidateRequest, leaving seven named seams.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Create one DIRECT and one SOURCE-BACKED proposal. Exercise each named seam against both rows, then query the row through system.store.transaction() and a separate sqlite3 connection. Record per-path exposure counts and additional raw-storage routes.
rows.proposed: Treat the list as eight named high-level seams in the union, not an exhaustive security count and not eight per submission path. Add that qualifier and mention that authorized ledger access exposes every storage identifier by design.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED. Eight NAMED high-level seams in the union - not an exhaustive security count, and not eight per path. The DIRECT path never constructs a `CandidateRequest`. Authorized ledger access exposes every storage identifier by design.

rows.locus: private in M3.3 means a storage role the new API neither accepts nor returns
rows.divergence: Reading A defines 'new API' as the two public method signatures and their return values; reading B includes the callback boundary to caller-supplied CandidateSource code, where D14 deliberately hands over the request ID. Only A is consistent with D14.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Inspect both signatures and results, then use a recording source. Confirm neither method accepts request_id and neither result equals it, while CandidateRequest.request_id still reaches the adapter and equals the persisted requests.id.
rows.proposed: The contract mandates reading A. Describe the ID as internal plumbing absent from the two method signatures/results, not as private from adapters, existing readers, reviewers, or authorized storage access.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED, reading A. 'Private' names a STORAGE ROLE the two signatures neither accept nor return. It is not privacy from adapters, from existing readers, or from the ledger.

rows.locus: no shipped sentence may state or imply that M3.3 removed request identity
rows.divergence: Reading A permits precisely scoped prose such as 'submit_proposal accepts no request ID'; reading B bans any request-ID-free wording because a reader could infer system-wide removal. The prohibition on implication has no explicit audience or textual domain.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Present the shipped sentence 'The submission methods neither accept nor return a request ID; schema-v2 still stores and existing readers expose one.' Reading A accepts its bounded claim, while a lexical reading B rejects it merely for containing the first clause.
rows.proposed: Permit method-scoped absence claims only when the same passage states that schema-v2 retains the row and existing surfaces expose its ID. Ban unqualified claims that Cement or M3.3 removed, hid, or made request identity opaque.
rows.main_verdict: CONFIRMED. A method-scoped absence claim is permitted only when the same passage states that schema v2 retains the row and existing surfaces expose its ID. README and architecture.md now carry exactly that pairing. Unqualified removal claims stay banned.
rows.contract_action: section 11; the executable prose battery is D30/S3 work

rows.locus: decisive gate reaches 635 + N tests with zero failures
rows.divergence: Reading A accepts unittest's exit 0 and zero failures/errors even when an M3.3 test is skipped; reading B treats 'reaches' as requiring every added test to execute. A deliberately skipped test increments the reported count and still prints OK.
rows.distinguishing_probe: Add one @unittest.skip M3.3 test to a 635-test baseline and run the exact decisive command. Observe 'Ran 636 tests' and exit 0 with OK (skipped=1); compare that with a requirement that N added tests have zero skips.
rows.proposed: Require 635 + N discovered tests, zero failures and errors, and zero skips among M3.3-added tests. Existing unrelated skips, if any, need their own baseline rather than silently satisfying a new obligation.
rows.main_verdict: SCOPED and MEASURED. 635 + N DISCOVERED tests, zero failures, zero errors, and zero skips AMONG THE TESTS M3.3 ADDS - a skipped test increments the count and still prints OK. Measured 668 tests, 0 failures, 0 errors, 206.045 s.

rows.locus: the read-site census counts are a TRIPWIRE; violations == [] is the load-bearing assertion
